Interval walking simply means alternating between slower and faster walking for set amounts of time. It gives your walk a bit of structure and keeps things interesting. You don’t need to sprint; just pick up the pace when it’s “fast” and ease off when it’s “slow.” We’ll guide you through each phase so you can focus on the walk.
Why choose interval walking over steady walking or running?

Mixing easier and harder efforts can help improve fitness without feeling like you have to push the whole time. It’s also gentler on the joints than running for many people. Research suggests that when you burn similar energy, walking and running can offer comparable heart and metabolic benefits, so you’re not missing out by walking.
How do notifications work in this app?

You’ll get a gentle vibration (and optional voice) when it’s time to switch phases. While a workout is running, we also show a small notification so Android keeps the session going in the background. That way you can switch apps or lock the phone and jump back in whenever you’re ready.
Can I change the voice used for announcements?

Yes. In Settings under Workout, turn on Voice Notifications if needed, then tap \"Voice\" to pick a language from supported options. Choose \"Default\" to use the system default voice. Availability depends on your device’s TTS engine and installed voices for each language.
Which languages are supported for voice announcements?

We support localized announcements for Arabic, Danish, Dutch, Filipino, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Korean, Malayalam, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), Russian, Simplified Chinese (China), Spanish, Swedish, Tagalog, Tamil, Telugu, Thai, Traditional Chinese (Hong Kong), Turkish, Urdu, and Vietnamese, with English as the default. These translations were AI-generated and may contain mistakes. Actual availability depends on your device’s TTS engine and installed voices.
Can workouts run in the background?

Yes. On supported Android versions, your workout keeps going when you switch away or lock the phone. We use a small notification so the system doesn’t stop us. If you have an older device or strict battery saver on, excluding this app from battery optimization in system settings often helps everything run smoothly.
How do I choose a formula?

The 3-3 Japanese option is the classic default (about 30 minutes). If you want something shorter and punchier, try 5-2 High Intensity; for a longer session with a three-phase pattern, 5-4-5 Circuit is great. Design Your Own lets you set your own slow/fast times, number of rounds, and whether you’d like to start slow or fast.
What is Interval Mode vs Circuit Mode?

Interval Mode is the simple one: just slow and fast, over and over for as many rounds as you pick. Circuit Mode adds a third phase each round (e.g. Fast → Slow → Fast / Slow → Fast → Slow), so you get a bit more variety. You can switch between them in Design Your Own using the Training Type toggle.

We don’t measure your speed; you’re in charge of your pace. As a guide, \"slow\" is ideally around 4/10 effort (comfortable) and \"fast\" around 7/10 (brisk but not exhausting). The app just keeps time and lets you know when to switch.
Where is my custom formula saved?

Right now we save only the state of your custom formula: the slow/fast times, rounds, and options you had set the last time you used Design Your Own and tapped Create. That’s restored when you reopen the app. A future release will let you save and manage multiple custom formulas.
Can I pause or reset during a workout?
Absolutely. You can Pause (then Resume) or Reset whenever you need to. We only add a workout to your history when you finish it, so if you pause or reset, that session won’t be counted. No pressure.
What is the countdown and how do I change it?
It’s a short “get ready” delay (1–10 seconds) before the workout begins, with optional voice and haptic cues. You can turn it on or off and pick how many seconds in Settings under Workout.

When Save Workouts is on (in Settings or Workout History), we save each workout you complete. You’ll get a calendar, totals, streaks, and per-day details. You can turn saving off anytime, delete individual workouts from a day’s detail, or clear all history from the Workout History screen. It’s all up to you.
Is my data stored or shared online?
Nope. Everything stays on your device, including your workout history. No accounts, no cloud sync, and we don’t share anything with anyone. For the full picture, check out our Privacy Policy.
Why does the app ask for \"Physical activity\" or notifications?

We need notifications to show that a workout is in progress so it can keep running when you’re not in the app. Android also asks for \"Physical activity\" for that type of background workout. We use it only so the workout can continue; we don’t read your steps or any movement data.
Why does my workout stop when I lock my phone or switch apps?

First, check that notifications are enabled for the app and you’ve said yes to \"Physical activity\" if Android asked. On some devices, telling the system not to battery-optimize this app (in system settings) makes a big difference. Worth trying if the workout keeps stopping.

When it’s on, the screen stays on while you’re in the app so you can glance at the timer. When you lock the phone, the workout keeps running either way. That’s handled separately, so you’re good to go with the screen off.
Is interval walking safe for me?

We’re just a timer. You decide how hard to push. If you have any health concerns, it’s always a good idea to check with your doctor before starting a new exercise routine. Our Terms of Service has the full disclaimer.
